steps.body: Any linear equation falls into exactly three cases. Simplify both sides, then look: if x survives with a real value, ONE solution; if x cancels leaving a true statement, INFINITELY MANY; if x cancels leaving a false statement, NONE.

widget.prompt: You solve an equation and reach x = 7. How many solutions?

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Right — a real value for x means exactly one solution.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: You found an actual x-value (7), so there IS a solution — exactly one.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: A single value like x = 7 is one solution, not infinitely many — that would need the x to cancel into a true statement.

options.label: It depends on x
options.feedback: x = 7 pins it down to exactly one solution, no dependence.

predict.prompt: Which ending signals an equation with NO solution — 'x = 7' or '0 = 5'?
predict.reveal: When the x's vanish and what's left is FALSE, no number could ever fix it — zero solutions. A leftover truth like 7 = 7 means every number works instead.

steps.body: A quick shortcut: compare the simplified x-coefficients. DIFFERENT coefficients always give one solution (the lines cross). SAME coefficients give either none or infinitely many, decided by whether the constants match.

explanationVariants: 2x + 5 = 3x − 1 has different x-coefficients (2 vs 3), so exactly one solution.
Different coefficients → the x survives → one solution.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Right — the x-coefficients differ (2 vs 3), so x survives with one value.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The coefficients differ (2x vs 3x), so the x does NOT cancel — this has one solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs identical sides — here the coefficients differ, giving one solution.

options.label: Two solutions
options.feedback: A linear equation never has exactly two — different coefficients give one solution.

explanationVariants: 7x + 2 = 7x + 2 has identical sides, so infinitely many solutions.
Same coefficient AND same constant → infinitely many.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Right — identical sides mean every x works.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: The sides are identical, so x cancels into 2 = 2 (always true) — infinitely many, not one.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: That needs different constants — here they match (2 = 2), so infinitely many.

options.label: x = 2
options.feedback: Every x works, not only 2 — infinitely many solutions.

widget.prompt: Sort each equation by its number of solutions.

items.label: 6x + 1 = 6x + 7
items.feedback: Same coefficient, different constants (1 vs 7) — no solution.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — compare the x-coefficients first, then the constants if the coefficients match.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — different coefficients give one; same coefficients give none or infinitely many.

explanationVariants: 2(3x + 1) = 6x + 2 expands to 6x + 2 = 6x + 2 — identical, so infinitely many.
After distributing, both sides match exactly → infinitely many.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Right — distribute to 6x + 2 = 6x + 2, identical sides: every x works.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: After distributing, both sides are 6x + 2 — identical, so infinitely many, not one.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The constants match after distributing (2 = 2), so infinitely many, not none.

options.label: x = 2
options.feedback: Every x works — the sides are identical, giving infinitely many solutions.

explanationVariants: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6 distributes to 3x + 6 = 3x + 6 — identical, so infinitely many solutions.
Distribute and compare: both sides become 3x + 6, giving infinitely many.

options.label: Infinitely many solutions
options.feedback: Right — distribute to 3x + 6 = 3x + 6, identical sides: every x works.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Distributing gives 3x + 6 on both sides — identical, so infinitely many, not one.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The constants match (6 = 6) after distributing, so infinitely many, not none.

options.label: Exactly three solutions
options.feedback: A linear equation is never exactly three — this one is infinitely many.

hints: Now compare: 3x + 6 = 3x + 6 — are the two sides identical?
They're identical, so the equation is true for every x: infinitely many solutions.

steps.body: Every linear equation has one, none, or infinitely many solutions — the leftover statement tells you which.
takeaways: Same coefficients, same constants → infinitely many.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: systems of two equations and their solutions.

concept.body: Classify a linear equation by simplifying: different x-coefficients → one solution; same coefficients with same constants → infinitely many; same coefficients with different constants → none.

explanationVariants: 3x + 2 = 5x − 4 has different coefficients (3 vs 5), so one solution.
Different coefficients → the x survives → one solution.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Right — different x-coefficients (3 vs 5) give exactly one solution.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The coefficients differ, so the x survives — one solution, not none.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs identical sides — here the coefficients differ, so one solution.

options.label: Zero
options.feedback: Different coefficients guarantee exactly one solution.
